firewall.detectHelp: Attacks are logged but still reach the site. Start here and read the log for false alarms.
firewall.blockHelp: A request the rules call an attack gets a 403 page and never reaches the site.
firewall.title: Web application firewall
firewall.help: Checks requests to PHP and apps against the OWASP Core Rule Set: SQL injection, cross-site scripting, file inclusion and more. Static files are not checked.
firewall.notInstalled: The firewall is not installed on this server (it needs libmodsecurity and the rules: {cmd}). The setting is kept and applies once it is.

siteProtection.title: Site Protection
siteProtection.intro: Ask for a password on a folder, stop PHP from running in upload folders, and stop other sites from embedding your images, accept traffic only through Cloudflare, and screen requests with a web application firewall. The edge gateway checks these before anything else answers.

folders.title: Password-protected folders
folders.help: Visitors to a folder (and everything under it) must sign in. Use {root} for the whole site. Certificate renewal is never blocked.
folders.addHelp: Adding an existing username again changes its password.

portShares.title: Port Share
portShares.subtitle: Serve a website, or a path of it, from a Node.js app, a Python app or any local port.
portShares.nothingHelp: Pick a website and a path, then a Node.js app, a Python app or any local port.
portShares.noWebsitesHelp: Create a website first; its domain is where the app is published.
portShares.noneShared: Nothing shared. The whole site is served by {label}.

form.subtitle: The edge gateway reverse-proxies the website path to an app or local port.
form.pathHelp: {root} hands the whole website to the app. A path like {example} sends only that part; the rest stays on {base}.
form.noApps: No {runtime} apps yet. {link}, or share a local port.
form.stripHelp: On for apps that expect to live at {root}.
form.previewNote: SSL, IP rules and redirects of the website still apply. Certificate checks under /.well-known/acme-challenge/ are never forwarded.
form.backendsHelp: Another server's address, e.g. http://192.168.0.106:80 or https://app.lan:8443. Add more than one to load balance; a backend that stops answering is skipped for 15 seconds.

policyHelp.round_robin: Each request goes to the next backend in turn.
policyHelp.ip_hash: A visitor always lands on the same backend, so logins and sessions keep working.
policyHelp.failover: Everything goes to the first backend; the others take over only while it is down.

form.preserveHost: Send the website's domain as Host
form.preserveHostHelp: On when the backend picks the site by domain name (nginx/Apache virtual hosts). Off sends the backend's own address.
form.verifyTlsHelp: Turn off only for https backends on your own network with a self-signed certificate.

subdomains.label: All subdomains
subdomains.help: Any name under {domain} (a.{domain}, b.{domain}…) uses this website and its shares, unless that subdomain has a website of its own. Point a *.{domain} DNS record at this server.
subdomains.needWildcardSsl: HTTP works now. For HTTPS on subdomains, turn on Wildcard SSL for this website (Websites → SSL).

tpl.httpsDesc: Always redirect HTTP requests to HTTPS based on hostname.
tpl.wwwDesc: Always redirect requests from the WWW subdomain to the root (also known as the “apex” or “naked” domain).
tpl.domainDesc: Redirect all requests to a different hostname using HTTPS, keeping the original path and query string.

redirects.title: Redirect Rules
redirects.subtitle: Redirects answered by the edge gateway before your site is reached.
redirects.emptyHelp: Start from a template: HTTPS, www to root, or a different domain.
redirects.noWebsitesHelp: Create a website first, then add redirect rules to it.
redirects.noneHere: No redirect rules on this website.
redirects.noSsl: This website has no SSL certificate yet. Issue one before turning on HTTPS redirects.
redirects.taken: This website already has this rule. Edit the existing one instead.
redirects.name: Rule name
redirects.previewNote: The path is always kept. Certificate checks under /.well-known/acme-challenge/ are never redirected.
